nodes.label: E-Gen: E-Graph-Based Mathematical Expression Dataset Generation
nodes.author: Hongbo Zheng, Suyuan Wang, Neeraj Gangwar, Nickvash Kani
nodes.rationale: Novel corpus generation scheme using e-graphs to synthesize large, diverse mathematical expression datasets. Addresses limitations of SymPy-based methods by enabling 102-average cluster size (vs. 2 for prior work) and 34 operators (vs. 24). Embedding models trained on E-Gen outperform GPT-4o on mathematical reasoning tasks.

nodes.label: E-Graph Data Structure
nodes.rationale: Advanced data structure for efficiently manipulating collections of terms under congruence relation. Enables saturation by applying ~800 mathematical rules to generate clusters of semantically equivalent expressions. E-classes contain equivalent e-nodes; edges connect e-nodes to child e-classes representing operator arguments.

nodes.label: Seq2Seq Equivalent Expression Generation
nodes.rationale: Training approach where encoder learns to map input expressions into latent space by predicting mathematically equivalent expressions as output. Achieves 96.72% accuracy on K-means clustering of equivalent expressions, outperforming SEMEMB (37.70%).

nodes.label: Contrastive Learning for Expression Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Representation learning approach using InfoNCE loss to embed semantically equivalent expressions closer together while pushing distinct expressions apart. CL Mean achieves 97.61% clustering accuracy; enables learning of latent space where mathematical semantics are captured.

nodes.label: Mathematical Language Processing Downstream Tasks
nodes.rationale: Evaluation tasks including K-means clustering, semantic understanding beyond syntactic similarity, mistake detection in derivations, and embedding algebra (mathematical analogies). E-Gen models outperform SEMEMB and GPT-4o across all tasks.

nodes.label: Mistake Detection in Mathematical Derivations
nodes.rationale: Out-of-distribution task evaluating whether embeddings capture semantic information to identify erroneous steps in mathematical derivations. Seq2seq achieves 77.99% F1 on mistake detection vs. SEMEMB's 53.61%, demonstrating robustness and generalizability.

nodes.label: Embedding Algebra Task
nodes.rationale: Analogy-based reasoning task extending word2vec-style operations to mathematical expressions. Given triplet (x1, y1, x2), predict y2 such that x1:y1 :: x2:y2. Seq2seq achieves 70.38% accuracy vs. GPT-4o's 39.60%, indicating superior understanding of mathematical transformations.

nodes.label: Mathematical Semantics in Continuous Vector Space
nodes.rationale: Learning continuous representations of symbolic mathematical expressions that capture semantic equivalence beyond syntactic similarity. E-Gen corpus enables models to learn underlying mathematical rules through diverse transformations. Embeddings support downstream tasks: clustering, mistake detection, analogical reasoning.
